Question: Two different prime numbers between \(4\) and \(18\) are chosen. When their sum is subtracted from their product, which of the following numbers could be obtained?
Solution:
The prime numbers between \(4\) and \(18\) are \(5,7,11,13,17\). Since swapping the two chosen primes does not change the result, call the smaller one \(p\) and the larger one \(q\).

Group the pairs by \(p\), using each larger eligible prime for \(q\). The values of \(pq-(p+q)\), with \(q\) increasing in each row, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
p=5:&\quad23,39,47,63,\\
p=7:&\quad59,71,95,\\
p=11:&\quad119,159,\\
p=13:&\quad191.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every distinct pair appears exactly once because it has a unique smaller member. Among the answer choices, only \(119\) occurs. In particular, choosing \(11\) and \(13\) gives
\[
11\cdot13-(11+13)=143-24=\boxed{119}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
